issues.description: The problem statement uses a different method name style for the total-students method: it refers to get_total_number_of_students() (snake_case) in the task description, while the UML, template comments, and solution use getTotalNumberOfStudents() (camelCase). This naming/signature mismatch can confuse students about the exact method name they should implement and may lead to inconsistent implementations or failing tests that expect the camelCase name.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all materials. Update the problem statement text to refer to getTotalNumberOfStudents() (camelCase) to match the UML, template TODO comments, and the solution. Alternatively, explicitly note that the intended method name is getTotalNumberOfStudents() to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The problem text uses a snake_case identifier `get_total_number_of_students()` (line 41) while the UML, template comments and the solution implement the Java-style camelCase method `getTotalNumberOfStudents()`. This inconsistency can confuse students about the exact method name to implement in Java and may lead them to try to implement a non-idiomatic or mismatched identifier.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier naming in the problem statement to use the camelCase Java convention. Replace `get_total_number_of_students()` with `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` in the problem text so it matches the UML, template comments and the solution implementation.
